Technology stocks were posting small gains as a group in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.2% in value although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was slipping slightly more than 0.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Electronic Arts ( EA ) retreated Thursday, at one point falling over 9%, after it reduced its outlook for FY19 net bookings by about $350 million to around $5.2 billion, in part to reflect a four-week delay in the upcoming launch of its highly-anticipated 'Battlefield V' video game. The game will be released on Nov. 20 instead of Oct. 23, the company said in a statement, explaining the later date will allow it "to deliver the best possible experience for gamers." It also said about $115 million - or roughly one-third - of the lower expected bookings this year was driven by recent changes in foreign exchange rates.
In other sector news:
(+) Apple ( AAPL ) was almost 1% higher during Thursday trading following reports it purchased Akonia Holographics, a startup company specializing in making waveguide lenses - thin, transparent smart glass lenses that display vibrant, full-color, wide field-of-view images - for augmented reality glasses. Akonia owns over 200 patents in the holographic space and many see the acquisition as a sign Apple is venturing into the consumer AR headset business, according to a Reuters report. Neither Apple nor Akonia would comment on the transaction. Financial terms and other details also were not disclosed.
(-) Heico ( HEI ) was trading lower Thursday, dropping almost 1% to reverse a like-sized advance earlier in the session that followed the electronic components manufacturer saying it has acquired 100% of the business and assets of privately held Optical Display Engineering. Financial terms of the all-cash transaction were not disclosed, although Heico said its expects the deal will add to its per-share earnings during the first year after closing.
